newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Canadian arrested in Caymans in lotto scam.
newsitem.headline: Canadian arrested in Caymans in lotto scam.

text.p: A Canadian was arrested in an international sweepstakes scam in the United States and Canada, Cayman authorities said.
Pietro Paolo Codispoti, 32, of St. Hubert, Quebec, was arrested and charged with money laundering on Wednesday as he attempted to leave this British territory in the western Caribbean.

Codispoti was the courier in a scam that targeted elderly people, who were told they had won the Canadian national lottery but would have to pay a 7 percent tax up front before they could collect the grand prize, crown counsel Cheryl Richards said.
The "winners" were told to send a check to a Canadian postal address. The checks then were diverted to Grand Cayman to hide the money, Richards said.

Codispoti, who arrived in the Cayman Islands on April 29, collected the checks, deposited them in a Cayman bank, then rerouted the money to the Turks & Caicos islands in an effort to further conceal the money trail, she said.
About $25,000 was recovered, but the group could have ripped off hundreds of thousands of dollars from "winners," sources close to the investigation said.
"The magnitude of the scam is clearly not revealed by the arrest of this defendant," Richards said.
Cayman authorities said they had notified the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation and investigations were under way in both countries.
Codispoti was held without bail. Trial was set for May 20.

The Cayman Islands, an upscale tourist destination and tax haven, became a focal point of another international scandal last week when it was revealed that John Felderhof, a former top officer of Canadian gold exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd was living here and would not return to Canada in the near future.
Felderhof was head of mining and geology for Bre-X, which last year claimed to have found in Indonesia one of the richest lodes of gold in history.

After a spectacular stock market ride, Bre-X's claim was debunked by independent analysts, the company's stock tumbled and it declared bankruptcy, sparking investigations in the United States and Canada.
